thread.title: Goldman Sachs splits from the pack when it comes to playing political faves

author: Shawn Langlois
title: Goldman Sachs splits from the pack when it comes to playing political faves
text:
Democrats may be outnumbered in Washington D.C.’s corridors of power these days, but when it comes to drawing political cash from Corporate America over the past decade, the blue team rules by a rather large margin.
With one big exception. 
Cost-estimating website HowMuch.net crunched Federal Election Commission data from 250,000 of the country’s biggest companies going back to 2007 to create this chart of the 30 most politically active companies in the Fortune 500. 
Of note, these donations are from employees, not the companies themselves.
As you can see, Goldman Sachs GS, +0.50% tops the list by a wide margin, with its employees leaning slightly Republican. Morgan Stanley MS, +1.32% however, is the only other company in the top 10 to put more money into GOP coffers than into the hands of the left.
Interestingly, Charles Schwab SCHW, +0.74% splits from its fellow banking institutions with 70% of its donations spent on Democratic candidates.
“Republicans received more than 50% of the donations from only nine of the 30 companies, most of which tend to be grouped toward the bottom,” HowMuch.net’s Raul Amoros wrote. “Ultimately, it is fair to say that employees of these big companies have spent the bulk of their political cash on Democrats over the last decade.”
Other big supporters of the left include Microsoft MSFT, +0.59% at 80% and Apple AAPL, +0.49% at 88%. Facebook FB, -5.43% leads the way at 91%. 
Amoros also pointed out that utilities like Comcast CMCSA, -1.13% and AT&T T, -0.33% have a vested interest in the net neutrality debate , while Boeing BA, +1.89% and Lockheed Martin LMT, +0.47% rely on government contracts for business.
“In short, what’s a couple billion dollars spent on a political campaign if it means the government will stay out of your way?” he said. “Political contributions might be one of the smartest investments some workers can make for their own job security.”
